canonical_statement: The study aimed to investigate the sensation of dyspnea in hypoxemic emergency admissions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The aim of this study was to investigate the sensation of dyspnea in hypoxemic emergency admissions.

canonical_statement: All emergency admissions to the respiratory care unit at Siloah Hospital between October 1 and November 1, 2020 were analyzed retrospectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All emergency admissions to the respiratory care unit ... between October 1 and November 1, 2020, were analyzed retrospectively.

canonical_statement: Patients were included if supplementary oxygen was required within the first 24 hours after admission to achieve an SpO2 of at least 92%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with hypoxemia defined as supplementary oxygen demand to achieve an oxygen saturation (SpO2) ≥ 92% in the first 24 h after admission were included.

population.label: Hypoxemic respiratory admissions requiring supplemental oxygen
inclusion_criteria: Supplementary oxygen demand within 24 hours to achieve SpO2 ≥92%

canonical_statement: All included patients received SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing on admission.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing on admission.

canonical_statement: Perceived dyspnea was rated with the modified Borg CR10 scale, which the paper describes as having 12 stages from 0 to 10 including 0.5 and relating numbers to dyspnea during exertion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Subjects rated their perceived dyspnea using the modified Borg CR10 scale ... This scale has 12 stages from 0 to 10 including 0.5.

concept.text: Modified Borg CR10 perceived dyspnea rating

outcome.definition: 12-stage scale from 0 to 10 including 0.5; described by authors as relating to dyspnea during exertion

canonical_statement: Continuous variables were summarized as medians with 25th and 75th percentiles; categorical variables as n (%), with chi-square or Fisher exact tests for categorical variables and Student testing for metric variables after normality assessment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Continuous variables were described as median and 25 and 75% quartiles. Categorical variables are presented as n (%).

canonical_statement: A logistic regression model used Borg CR10 ≥5 as the categorical outcome, with variables selected for inclusion when univariate p was <0.1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A logistic regression model was fitted with a Borg CR10 scale of ≥5 as the categorical outcome. Variables included were identified by a p value of <0.1 in univariate analysis.

canonical_statement: The cohort included 82 patients: 45 (55%) with SARS-CoV-2 detected by PCR and 37 (45%) in the non-COVID-19 group.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: During the study period, 82 patients were included. In 45/82 (55%) patients, SARS-CoV-2 was detected by PCR on admission.

canonical_statement: Chronic respiratory disease was present in 9/45 (20%) COVID-19 patients versus 28/37 (76%) non-COVID-19 patients (p<0.001).

canonical_statement: In Table 2, COVID-19 was associated with markedly lower odds of Borg CR10 ≥5: OR 0.007 (95% CI 0.000-0.199; p=0.004).
In Table 2, pCO2 was not statistically associated with Borg CR10 ≥5: OR 0.816 per reported model unit (95% CI 0.627-1.061; p=0.129).
In Table 2, pH <7.35 was associated with higher odds of Borg CR10 ≥5: OR 95.816 (95% CI 1.744-5263.453; p=0.026).

The Results narrative separately reports that “silent hypoxemia,” defined there as Borg CR10 ≥5, was independently associated with COVID-19 and severe hypocapnia with OR 0.221 (95% CI 0.054-0.907; p=0.036).

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In multivariate analysis, silent hypoxemia as defined by the dyspnea Borg CR10 scale ≥5 was independently associated with COVID-19 and presence of severe hypocapnia with an odds ratio of 0.221 (95% confidence interval 0.054, 0.907, p 0.036).

outcome.definition: Definition reproduced exactly as reported in Results narrative

canonical_statement: The authors conclude that silent hypoxemia is more common in COVID-19 patients than in pulmonary patients with acute hypoxemia and that its uniqueness and pathophysiologic mechanisms need further evaluation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Silent hypoxemia is more common in COVID-19 patients compared to pulmonary patients with acute hypoxemia. Further evaluation of its uniqueness and pathophysiologic mechanisms is needed.

canonical_statement: The authors identify the single-center design and small number of participants, with consequent lack of subgroup analysis, as limitations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The series has potential limitation from the unicenter design with a small number of participants and a following lack of subgroup analysis.

canonical_statement: Virus variants were not screened in routine clinical care at the time of the study.
